alerts.title: Missing Viral Load Monitoring Plan
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring 3 months after ART initiation for pregnant women. Patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago and is 22 weeks pregnant, placing her near the 3-month mark. No clinician plan is documented to schedule this required test. Her viral load is 89 copies/mL, indicating good initial response, but ongoing monitoring is critical in pregnancy.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule a viral load test now, as it is approximately 3 months post-ART initiation during pregnancy.

alerts.title: Potential DTG-Iron Interaction
alerts.message: Guidelines note a potential interaction between dolutegravir (DTG) and divalent cation-containing medications like iron supplements. The patient is pregnant and taking ferrous sulfate. This interaction can reduce DTG absorption and efficacy. No plan documents addressing this interaction, such as advising staggered dosing.

evidence.recommended_action: Advise patient to take ferrous sulfate at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after DTG.

alerts.title: Rising Creatinine on TDF
alerts.message: Patient's creatinine has risen from 0.8 mg/dL (pre-ART baseline) to 1.1 mg/dL after 10 weeks on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF). TDF is a known cause of renal toxicity. The eGFR of 78 mL/min/1.73m2 indicates mild impairment. Non-drug causes like pregnancy-related physiological changes should also be considered, but the trend warrants attention.

evidence.recommended_action: Monitor renal function closely; consider more frequent creatinine and urine protein checks given pregnancy.
